conceptZh: 扭蛋小怪獸在夜燈下玩躲貓貓，筆畫一個個從角落探出頭又縮回去。
object: a fuzzy gachapon creature with a toy night-lamp
morph: strokes of 夜 sneak in from corners, dodge the creature under lamp light, then settle
creativeAngle: 躲貓貓：夜燈一閃，筆畫就躲。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a pale periwinkle background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 夜 as the only text on screen, drawn in warm amber solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a round fuzzy mint creature bursts out of a capsule and bounces off a small toy night-lamp, which blinks on; the first 夜 is spoken as the top lid-like 亠 stroke peeks in from the upper edge and ducks away. 1.7-3.4s: the lamp flickers and the remaining strokes dart in from different corners, dodging as the creature leaps at them and bounces off the walls; the second 夜 is spoken as it pins the last piece with a belly flop and everything snaps into the glyph. 3.4-5s: 夜市 is spoken as a string of paper lanterns and a tiny toy food cart with steam pop up on the horizon behind the glyph (animated shapes only). 5-8s: hold; the creature spins up a firefly, giggling, glyph still. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "夜、夜、夜市" (ㄧㄝˋ、ㄧㄝˋ、ㄧㄝˋ ㄕˋ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 夜 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.

conceptZh: 桶子海盜想抓高高掛著的月亮金幣，鸚鵡偏偏一腳踩歪大砲，把海盜轟得在地板、牆壁、天花板和積木小隊頭頂連環彈跳，每撞一下就喀啦敲進兩筆，最後一跳跌坐在倒成小凳子的積木上，夜字完整亮在旁邊，小夜市攤子跟著冒出來。
object: a barrel-shaped toy pirate fired from a toy cannon, a dangling gold moon-coin, a stubborn parrot, and a marching squad of building bricks
morph: each ricochet of the bouncing pirate (floor, wall, ceiling, brick-tower head) clacks two strokes of 夜 into place in standard stroke order, until the glyph stands complete and still beside him
creativeAngle: 前一版是安靜的躲貓貓與燈籠飄升，這版改成完全看得懂的物理連環彈跳：想要、失手、連撞四下、坐穩收尾，四個段落各不相同。鸚鵡踩歪大砲是「不合作」性格的具體笑點，積木小隊只當被撞的塔和最後的小凳子，不搶戲。夜字八筆分四次兩筆兩筆敲進，保證筆畫順序與結構正確，收尾海盜坐在字旁而非字上，避免遮住筆畫。單字「夜市」用冒出的小攤車和燈籠串具體呈現，與語音同步。
promptEn:
An 8-second animated slapstick clip. Stage: a flat pale lavender-blue dusk backdrop with a soft cream floor, bright and clean, nothing busy behind. The only text ever on screen is one Traditional Chinese glyph 夜, built in thick saturated tangerine strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins, standard form: a dot over a horizontal bar on top, below left a slanting stroke and a vertical (亻), below right a slant, a horizontal fold, a small dot inside, and a long right-falling sweep.

0–1.5s: a barrel-shaped toy pirate (wooden-barrel body, stubby legs, red bandana, tiny hook hand) stands at lower left, staring up at a shiny gold moon-coin dangling on a string at top center. He points at it with the hook and wiggles with greed. His green parrot yawns, flaps off his head and perches on the coin's string, deliberately unhelpful. From the right, a squad of chunky building bricks marches in and stacks itself into a wobbly tower.

1.5–3s: the pirate squeezes into a little toy cannon aimed at the coin and gives a thumbs-up. The parrot swoops down and stamps one foot on the barrel, tilting it straight at the floor. Soft POP. The pirate blasts downward, squashes flat on the floor and BOINGS back up. As he hits, the first 夜 is spoken and the top dot and horizontal bar clack into place.

3–4.5s: a fast bounce chain, each hit with a satisfying clack and a stretch-and-squash: left wall, the slant and vertical of 亻 snap in; ceiling, the right slant and horizontal fold snap in; then he bonks the brick tower's top brick, the small dot and long falling sweep snap in and the glyph is complete. The second 夜 is spoken on that last bonk. The brick tower wobbles and topples, landing as a neat little stool just right of the glyph.

4.5–5.5s: the pirate plops down onto the brick stool, dizzy spiral eyes and a huge grin. The moon-coin drops into his lap. Right then the word 夜市 is spoken, and a tiny toy night-market food cart with a swaying string of paper lanterns and a puff of steam pops up in the lower right corner, small and clear of the glyph.

5–8s: hold. The glyph 夜 stays perfectly still and fully readable in the center. Beside it the pirate fans himself with his bandana, the lanterns sway gently, and the parrot finally lands, on the tip of his nose, making him go cross-eyed.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly these syllables, slowly and distinctly with clear tones: 夜、夜、夜市 (ㄧㄝˋ、ㄧㄝˋ、ㄧㄝˋ ㄕˋ), a short pause between the two single characters, and stops after the word. No other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Cartoon clacks and boings only, gentle, under the voice. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
